free_tier.stated: No published total-storage quota and no published per-snap byte cap; the practical ceiling is what the upload tooling survives. Evidence of real large artefacts: `kicad` stable snap is 1,659.5 MB and `android-studio` is 1,657.8 MB in the channel map (both served fine). A 5.5 GB upload attempt returned HTTP 500 and was diagnosed by Canonical as 'a timeout in the object storage load balancers'. 1.7 GB is documented as working; ~5 GB class uploads fail with a server-side timeout.

retention.stated: per-object-cap: not documented, empirically ~1.7 GB works and 5.5 GB 500s (object-storage load-balancer timeout). retention: indefinite, full revision history retained (each revision is a separate stored .snap)

egress.terms: Free and CDN-backed. Downloads go through api.snapcraft.io -> redirect -> a CDN; no billing, no per-download accounting.

tooling: `snapcraft upload` / `snapcraft push` (the write path), Snap Store API v2 (`api.snapcraft.io/v2/snaps/info/<name>` with header `Snap-Device-Series: 16`) for metadata, and plain HTTPS GET of the channel-map `download.url` for bytes. No rclone backend; a wrapper would have to speak the snapcraft upload protocol to push.
chaining: unlimited snaps per publisher account x unlimited revisions per snap (revision history is retained server-side - the forum thread discusses 3 GB across 3 revisions of a 1 GB game). Multiply by unlimited free Ubuntu One accounts. Realistically ~1.6 GB x N revisions x N snaps, but upload reliability degrades well before 5 GB.
limits_note: per-object-cap: not documented, empirically ~1.7 GB works and 5.5 GB 500s (object-storage load-balancer timeout). retention: indefinite, full revision history retained (each revision is a separate stored .snap). request-rate: not documented. A 'FATAL ERROR: Data queue size is too large' error hits multi-GB uploads client-side too.
reliability_note: The write path is the weak link, not storage: multi-GB uploads fail with opaque HTTP 500 ('timeout in the object storage load balancers') and with client-side 'Data queue size is too large'. Bytes are served perfectly once published (`200 77574144 application/octet-stream` verified). Snaps are squashfs images - arbitrary content must be packaged into a snap with a valid snapcraft.yaml, so this is a wrapper-only route.
